rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for someone who is easily irritated or short-tempered.

example.english: They’re really tetchy; even the slightest thing can make them lose their temper.

rows.note: Use this for a cranky or irritable person, especially when their mood makes them unpleasant to be around.

example.english: I don’t know what’s up with my son today—he’s so tetchy that everyone at home is avoiding him.

rows.note: Use this for the figurative sense of someone or something that is difficult to manage, work with, or use.

example.english: This old printer is really tetchy; it jams if you so much as move it.
